supported.quote: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's spend by the number of purchases flagged `in_current_month` and does not handle an empty list. So for a shopper who has bought before but not this month, it raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turns that error into a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Switching on a new monthly spending summary made the account page fail with a division by zero, likely for shoppers who had bought before but not yet this month.
Switching monthly-spend-feature back on before a fix is in place could make account pages fail again in the same way.
Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 during {G5309.3}. No such error was logged before then.

The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on by admin at {P1.1}. Before that it was evaluated off and account pages rendered normally. Evaluations were split between off and on at {G971b.6} and were all on during {Gce95.4}.
Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed only one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read.
With the flag on, account page requests reached a monthly per-item spend calculation that divides by zero for shoppers with no purchases this month.
The flag change reached all account page traffic almost at once: evaluations were split briefly and then all on. No staged rollout or health check that would hold back or undo a flag change was seen.
No test of the flag-on path for a shopper with past purchases but none this month was seen before the flag was switched on. Code-Fix says the cases it adds would raise against the current code.
Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident.
